context: git clean: -n previews, -d includes untracked directories, and -x also removes ignored files such as .env and local caches. Those are exactly the files with no copy in history, so -x deserves the preview most.
instruction: List untracked files a clean would remove, including ignored ones.

context: mv and cp accept --backup, where numbered keeps app.conf.~1~, app.conf.~2~ and so on. --backup=simple keeps only the most recent, suffixed with a tilde.
instruction: Overwrite a file but keep a copy of what was there.

context: ollama: list shows locally pulled models with their size and digest. ollama ps shows which are loaded into memory right now, which is the one that matters for VRAM pressure. ollama ships no man page.
instruction: List the models currently downloaded locally.

context: awk splits each line on runs of whitespace by default, numbering fields from $1, where $0 is the whole line. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored, unlike cut which counts every delimiter.
instruction: Print the third whitespace-separated column of a file.

context: GNU coreutils: md5sum prints the hash followed by two spaces and the filename. macOS instead has a command literally named md5 whose default output is a single-line 'MD5 (file) = hash' form.
instruction: Get the MD5 hash of an ISO image to compare against a published value.

context: rsync: -n is the dry run and prints the transfer list without touching anything. --delete removes destination files absent from the source, so previewing it is not optional.
instruction: Preview exactly what a mirroring sync would change before running it.

context: curl: -v prints request and response headers plus TLS negotiation on stderr, prefixed with > and <. --trace-ascii writes the full body exchange to a file when headers are not enough.
instruction: Debug a TLS or redirect problem by seeing the full exchange.

context: util-linux dmesg: --since applies a time boundary and --time-format iso renders wall-clock timestamps. Converted wall-clock times may be inaccurate across suspend and resume.
instruction: Show kernel messages from the last hour with ISO-style timestamps.

context: GNU date: prefixing a number with @ inside -d interprets it as seconds since the Unix epoch, and -u renders the result in UTC. BSD date spells this as -r with a bare number.
instruction: Convert the Unix timestamp 1700000000 to a readable UTC time.

context: df: -i reports inode usage rather than bytes, which is the explanation when writes fail at apparently low utilization. -h formats the counts with unit suffixes.
instruction: Diagnose a disk-full error when there is clearly free space.

context: BSD ping spells the overall deadline -t in seconds, while on Linux -t is the IP time-to-live and -W is the reply timeout. This flag means different things on each platform.
instruction: Bound a reachability check on macOS.

context: Zsh: zmv -n is a dry run that prints each intended rename without performing it. -i prompts per file and -f forces overwriting. Running -n first is the standard guard against a bad capture group.
instruction: Preview a bulk rename before actually moving anything.

context: docker: -f follows the stream and --tail limits the backlog. --since accepts a timestamp or a relative duration such as 10m for narrowing an incident window.
instruction: Follow the last hundred log lines of a running container.

context: sysstat sar: -n DEV selects network-device statistics, including packets and bytes received and transmitted per second. Other -n keywords report protocols, sockets, or errors instead.
instruction: Collect per-interface network throughput every two seconds for five reports.

context: sort: -k2,2 confines the key to field two, where a bare -k2 would extend to the end of the line. Attaching n and r to the key applies numeric and reverse ordering to that key only.
instruction: Sort a report numerically by its second column, largest first.

context: grep: -L prints files containing no match, which is how you audit for something absent. -l would print the files that already comply. --include limits the walk to matching basenames.
instruction: Find Python files under src that are missing a license header.

context: sed: two addresses separated by a comma form a range that starts at the first match and ends at the next match of the second, inclusive. d deletes every line in that range.
instruction: Strip an HTML comment block spanning several lines from a file.

context: tr: -s squeezes repeated occurrences of the character into one. tr reads only from stdin and never takes a filename argument, which is why the redirect is required.
instruction: Turn a space-aligned report into single-space-separated fields.

context: pgrep: -f matches against the entire command line rather than just the process name, which is required for interpreted scripts. -a prints the matched command alongside the PID.
instruction: Find the PID of a process by matching its full command line.

context: dd: verify of= names the intended device with lsblk immediately beforehand, because dd overwrites without confirmation and a wrong letter destroys the system disk. status=progress reports throughput and conv=fsync flushes before exit.
instruction: Write a disk image to a removable device and watch the progress.

context: Zsh: ** matches across directory levels, so **/*.py finds Python files at any depth including the current one. The dot qualifier drops anything that is not a regular file, which prevents a directory named like a source file from breaking the command.
instruction: Count the lines in every Python file anywhere below the current directory.

context: nl: -b sets the body numbering style, where a numbers all lines and t, the default, numbers only non-empty ones. This difference is why nl and cat -n disagree on files containing blank lines.
instruction: Number every line of a file including the blank ones.

context: jq: group_by sorts and buckets by the key expression, producing an array of arrays. map then reduces each bucket, where .[0] samples the shared key and length gives the bucket size.
instruction: Count records by their status field in a JSON Lines file.

context: openssl x509: -noout suppresses the re-encoded certificate so only the requested fields print. -text gives the full human-readable dump, and -fingerprint gives the hash used for pinning.
instruction: Read the subject and validity dates out of a certificate file.

context: base32 uses a case-insensitive alphabet with no easily confused characters, which is why TOTP seeds use it rather than base64. -d decodes and -w controls line wrapping as with base64.
instruction: Encode a secret in the format authenticator apps expect.

context: chmod: capital X sets the execute bit only on directories and on files that already have execute somewhere, unlike lowercase x which sets it on every file. This is the correct recursive repair.
instruction: Recursively fix a tree so directories are traversable but files do not become executable.

context: xargs: capital -I defines a replacement token and implies one command per input line. Lowercase -i is a deprecated alias that defaults the token to {}. -print0 and -0 pair up so filenames containing spaces survive the pipe.
instruction: Rename every .txt file under docs to .md, one invocation per file.

context: nohup makes the process ignore SIGHUP so a closing terminal does not kill it. Redirecting both streams is still needed, otherwise output lands in nohup.out in the current directory.
instruction: Start a long job that survives the terminal closing.

context: cut projects a single field and sort -u both orders and deduplicates in one pass, which is cheaper than piping into a separate uniq. -u compares the whole line here because no key was given.
instruction: List the distinct login shells configured on this machine.

context: Zsh: parentheses with a pipe express alternation inside a glob, matching either extension. Unlike brace expansion this only produces names that actually exist, so it never yields a nonexistent path.
instruction: List all the C and header files in this directory.

context: xargs: -a reads the argument list from a file instead of stdin. BatchMode=yes makes ssh fail immediately rather than blocking on a password prompt, which is essential when running unattended in parallel.
instruction: Check the uptime of every host listed in a file, four at a time.

context: kubectl: rollout status blocks until the rollout completes and exits non-zero on failure or timeout, which makes it usable as a deployment gate in CI. --timeout accepts Go duration strings such as 90s or 5m.
instruction: Wait until a deployment has finished rolling out.

context: BSD date: -v adjusts the date by a signed amount and a unit letter, so -v-7d means seven days earlier. The adjustment attaches directly to -v with no space. GNU's -d '7 days ago' is not accepted.
instruction: Print the date seven days ago in ISO format on macOS.

context: pip list --outdated queries the index for each package, so it is slow on large environments. --format=json suits scripting, and --not-required hides transitive dependencies.
instruction: See which installed packages have newer releases.

context: cargo: -p selects one workspace package and --test names an integration test target under tests/. Arguments after the bare -- are passed to the test harness, where --nocapture stops it from swallowing stdout.
instruction: Run one specific test in the syntax crate and show its printed output.

context: split: -l splits on line count, -d uses numeric rather than alphabetic suffixes, and --additional-suffix preserves the extension so downstream tools still recognise the format. The final argument is the output prefix.
instruction: Break a huge dataset into chunks of one million lines each.

context: Redirection is applied left to right: 2> sends stderr to the file, then > discards stdout. Reversing the order would point stderr at the terminal because 2>&1 semantics depend on what stdout referred to at that moment.
instruction: Capture only the warnings and errors from a build, discarding normal output.

context: macOS sort lacks GNU's -h, so du -sk emits a uniform kilobyte count that plain numeric -n can rank correctly. Mixing du -sh with sort -n instead compares the leading digits and puts 900M above 2G.
instruction: Rank the ten largest subdirectories by size on macOS.

context: BSD base64 spells decode with a capital -D where GNU uses lowercase -d, and takes its input file with -i rather than positionally. This is a frequent cause of scripts failing on macOS only.
instruction: Decode base64 on macOS.

context: cmake: -S is the source directory and -B the build directory, which keeps generated files out of the tree. Building afterwards is cmake --build build, portable across generators.
instruction: Configure an out-of-source release build.

context: macOS: lsof -i selects internet sockets and -sTCP:LISTEN narrows to listeners. -n skips DNS resolution and -P skips port-name lookup, which makes the output both faster and easier to grep. There is no ss on macOS.
instruction: Find which process is listening on TCP port 8080 on macOS.

context: sort: -h understands human-readable suffixes such as K, M, and G, so 2G sorts above 900M. Plain -n would compare the leading digits only and rank 900 above 2. du -s summarizes each argument and -h formats the size.
instruction: Show the largest directories under /var by size with human-readable units.

context: journalctl: -g applies a regular expression to MESSAGE and --case-sensitive=false explicitly enables case-insensitive matching. -b prevents old boots from adding unrelated matches.
instruction: Search current-boot journal messages case-insensitively for the phrase 'out of memory'.

context: psql: -1 wraps the file in a single transaction and ON_ERROR_STOP=1 aborts on the first error. Without both, psql continues past failures and commits each statement, leaving a half-applied migration.
instruction: Run a migration script so any error rolls the whole thing back.

context: macOS has no sha256sum; shasum -a selects the algorithm and its output format matches, so shasum -a 256 -c reads a GNU-generated manifest. The bare sha256 command exists too but formats differently.
instruction: Compute a SHA-256 checksum on macOS.

context: BSD sed supports -E for extended regular expressions just as GNU sed does, so capture groups port cleanly. What differs is -i, which on BSD requires a separate suffix argument.
instruction: Use a capture group in a substitution on macOS.

context: base64: GNU spells decode -d and BSD spells it -D, a case difference that breaks portable scripts. -i ignores non-alphabet characters such as embedded newlines.
instruction: Decode a base64 payload back to a file.

context: BSD xargs does not run the command when its input is empty, so the GNU -r flag is unnecessary here and is rejected by older macOS versions. The -0 and -print0 pairing still matters for filenames with spaces.
instruction: Delete matching files on macOS without erroring when nothing matches.
